findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses AND instead of OR, so team admins/owners can never add guests
findings.body: The permission check computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. `isTeamAdmin` checks membership role ADMIN and `isTeamOwner` checks role OWNER; a single membership cannot be both, so this expression is always false. Team admins and owners who are not themselves the booking host or an attendee will always hit the FORBIDDEN branch and cannot add guests to their team's bookings. This should be `||`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the booking host's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` loads the credentials of the user making the request, and the EventManager is built from those. But the calendar event being updated lives on the booking host's (organizer's) calendar. The handler explicitly allows attendees and (intended) team admins to add guests; in those cases the requester has no credential matching the booking's destination calendar/references, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` silently cannot update the calendar event — new guests are never added to the actual calendar/conferencing event. The query already includes `booking.user.credentials`; the EventManager should be constructed from the booking owner's credentials (as done elsewhere, e.g. using `booking.user`), not `ctx.user`.

findings.title: Any attendee can add an unlimited number of guests, enabling email spam through Cal.com's mailer
findings.body: The handler authorizes anyone whose email is among the booking's attendees (`isAttendee`) to add guests, and neither the schema nor the handler caps the number of guests per request or per booking. Combined with `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which sends an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to every new guest with the organizer's name in the From/Reply-To headers, any person who books (or is added to) a meeting can cause Cal.com to send branded invitation emails containing meeting details and links to arbitrary email addresses. This is a spam/phishing vector and can also blow up event attendee lists. Consider restricting this to the organizer/team admins, or at minimum enforcing a guest limit.

findings.title: Email comparisons are case-sensitive: blacklist bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: The filtering does `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not, so `USER@BLACKLISTED.COM` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. Likewise, adding `Foo@Bar.com` when attendee `foo@bar.com` already exists passes the uniqueness check and creates a duplicate attendee row (and duplicate emails). Normalize case before both comparisons.

findings.title: Schema does not enforce uniqueness of guests, allowing duplicate attendee rows
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts duplicates. The uniqueness refinement only exists client-side in AddGuestsDialog; anyone calling the tRPC mutation directly with `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` will pass validation, and `createMany` will insert two attendee rows for the same email (both also receiving invitation emails). Add a `.refine` for uniqueness (case-insensitive) in the schema or dedupe in the handler.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type settings that disable standard emails
findings.body: Every other send function in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` / `.host` via `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`/`eventTypeDisableHostEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no metadata parameter and unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees. Event types that disabled standard emails (e.g. because workflows replace them) will still send these notifications, producing duplicate/unwanted emails.

findings.title: Original (unfiltered) guest list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails
findings.body: The handler computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-registered attendees and blacklisted emails) but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, any existing attendee whose email appears in that raw list is treated as a "new guest" and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a fresh booking confirmation) instead of the "guests added" notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: No booking status/time validation: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking by id and only checks permissions; it never verifies `booking.status` or that the booking is in the future. The UI only exposes the action for confirmed upcoming bookings, but the mutation can be called directly to add guests to a cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-finished booking — inserting attendee rows and dispatching confirmation emails with calendar invites for an event that is cancelled or over. Reject non-ACCEPTED or past bookings.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar update, with no transaction or compensating path
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update(... createMany attendees ...)` commits the new attendees, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs afterwards outside any transaction. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails but the guests remain on the booking with no calendar invite and no email — and because the uniqueness filter now sees them as existing attendees, retrying the operation throws BAD_REQUEST ("emails_must_be_unique_valid"), leaving the guests permanently without invitations. Wrap in a transaction or send/update first and handle partial failure.

findings.title: Guests added to seated events get no seat reference, corrupting seat accounting
findings.body: The handler copies `seatsPerTimeSlot` into the event but always creates plain `Attendee` rows. For event types with seats, attendees are expected to be booked via `SeatReference` records, and remaining-seat availability is derived from seat bookings. Adding guests this way to a seated booking inflates the attendee list without consuming seats (allowing overbooking) and the new guests won't have the seat reference data other flows rely on. Seated event types should be rejected or handled via the seats flow.

findings.title: Initial state [""] makes Add with an untouched field show a validation error
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` initializes to `[""]`, so the `multiEmailValue.length === 0` guard in `handleAdd` is dead code and clicking Add without typing anything runs zod validation on an empty string, failing with the red "Emails must be unique and valid" error instead of being a no-op. Also, `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared when the user edits the email fields afterward, so the error stays visible until a successful submit or cancel. Initialize to `[]` (or filter empty strings before validating) and reset the error state on change.

findings.title: Email sending errors swallowed with console.log
findings.body: The `try/catch` around `sendAddGuestsEmails` logs `"Error sending AddGuestsEmails"` via `console.log` and discards the actual error object, then returns success to the client. Guests will appear added with no notification sent, users see a success toast, and operators get no usable log (the rest of the codebase uses `@calcom/lib/logger` and includes the error). At minimum log the error with the structured logger; ideally surface partial failure.
